subject: Plotting means of multiple factors from data set

messages.author: 3ffb5c32c053dc0b
messages.subject: Plotting means of multiple factors from data set
parts:
Hi all,
I have a dataset that contains the relative expression levels of three
genes, over 7 time points each. Additionally, I have multiple
replicates for each time point. I would like to find an efficient way
to plot the mean expression for each gene's time point (I would then
have a plot of three lines), with standard mean error bars.
Previously, I was doing the slow method of creating new data frames
for each gene, then finding the mean of each time point. I'm sure
there's an easier way to do this, such as quickly creating a vector of
all the means and standard errors. I feel like I'm getting close to
my goal by using melt and cast, but I'm really not sure. Here's what
I have:

dat=read.csv('http://dl.dropbox.com/u/1852742/relexpressions.csv')
datm=melt(dat)
#Rearrange time factors chronologically
datm$time=factor(datm
$time,levels=c('p4','p7','p14','p22','p28','p35','p50'))
#Target is the gene name
datm$target=factor(datm$target,levels=c('fgf2','fgf7','fgf10'))
#Creating data frames with the means and std errors
cast(datm,time~target~variable,subset=variable=='expression',mean)
stderr=function(data){sd(data)/sqrt(length(data))}
cast(datm,time~target~variable,subset=variable=='expression',stderr)

I don't know how to go from this point to actually plotting the means
and errors of each time point for each gene. Any advice would be
great. I appreciate your help!

-Jahan

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Plotting means of multiple factors from data set
parts:
Hi, probably this is a starting point:

mean_se <- function(x, mult = 1) {
x <- na.omit(x)
se <- mult * sqrt(var(x) / length(x))
mean <- mean(x)
data.frame(y = mean, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se)
}

ggplot(dat,aes(x=time,y=expression,
colour=target))+stat_summary(fun.data=mean_se)


--

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Plotting means of multiple factors from data set
parts:
Hi:

A different approach from Kohske's, using faceting:

dat$time <- factor(dat$time, levels = c('p4', 'p7', 'p14', 'p22', 'p28', 'p35', 'p50'))
dat$target <- factor(dat$target, levels = c('fgf2', 'fgf7', 'fgf10'))
dsumm <- ddply(dat, .(target, time), summarise,
                          meanxp = mean(expression, na.rm = TRUE),
                          sexp = sqrt(var(expression,
                               na.rm = TRUE)/length(expression[!is.na(expression)])))
ggplot(dsumm, aes(x = time, y = meanxp)) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = meanxp - sexp, ymax = meanxp + sexp), width = 0.2) +
      facet_wrap(~ target, nrow = 1)

# Aside: ----------------
I tried writing a simple function to do the standard error calculation, but ddply didn't like it:

stderr <- function(x) sqrt( var(x, na.rm = TRUE)/length(x[!is.na(x)]) )

ddply(dat, .(target, time), summarise,
                          meanxp = mean(expression, na.rm = TRUE),
                          sexp = stderr(expression) )
Error in stderr(expression) : unused argument(s) (expression)

The function returns a scalar, so I don't know why it chokes; even when used by itself (without the meanxp code) it returns the same error. (And I have the most recent version of everything on a Win7 64-bit system...)
#------------------------------

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Plotting means of multiple factors from data set
parts:
Hi:

Using my example dsumm from last time,

head(dsumm, 3)
  target time    meanxp      sexp
1   fgf2   p4  4.342000 0.6434134
2   fgf2   p7  6.109200 1.6678953
3   fgf2  p14 19.602000 6.1395791

geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = meanxp - sexp, ymax = meanxp + sexp), width = 0.3, size = 1) +
      geom_point() +
      geom_line(aes(group = 1), colour = 'blue') +

The trick is using aes(group = 1) to allow graphing lines across factor levels. Normally, geom_line() requires that the x variable be numeric, but Hadley created group = 1 to overcome that barrier.

@ Kohske: When I checked the help for stderr, it was a head slap moment :) I changed the name of the function to 'se' and now it works. Thanks for informing me of that.

HTH,
Dennis
